High-speed industrial collaborative arm launched at the 2026 Shanghai Industrial Expo. It reaches J6 joint speeds of up to 790°/s with ±0.02 mm repeatability, is IP67-rated and has internal cable routing.
12 kg version of Dobot's high-speed PULSA industrial cobot, with ±0.03 mm repeatability, IP67 protection and upright, inverted or side mounting.
Dual-arm teleoperation platform for collecting AI training data. It has two 6-axis arms with 625 mm reach, ±0.05 mm repeatability and ISO 15066 collision detection.

7-axis force-controlled adaptive collaborative robot from Shanghai-based Flexiv for contact-rich tasks such as precision assembly and polishing. Specs: 4 kg payload, 876 mm reach, ±0.05 mm repeatability, IP65. The Rizon robot was introduced in 2019.

6-axis collaborative robot from DOBOT's industrial CRA series, with a 5 kg payload, 900 mm reach and 0.02 mm repeatability. It is used for assembly, dispensing and material handling. The CRA series was unveiled at the Automate show in 2023.

Compact 6-axis collaborative robot from Suzhou-based Elite Robots' first EC series, with a 3 kg payload, 624 mm working radius, ±0.03 mm repeatability and 150 W typical power. The EC series (EC63/EC66/EC612) was ready for mass production in August 2018.

Mid-size 6-axis collaborative robot with a 6 kg payload, 914 mm working radius, ±0.03 mm repeatability and 250 W typical power. Its alpha version was built in 2017, and it entered mass production with the EC series in August 2018.
Large 6-axis collaborative robot in Elite Robots' EC series, with a 12 kg payload, 1,304 mm working radius, ±0.03 mm repeatability and 500 W power. It was ready for mass production in August 2018.
7-axis collaborative arm with joint torque sensing, integrated cameras and a ROS interface. Designed as a smaller, more precise successor to Baxter for machine tending and circuit-board testing.

Autonomous truck and trailer unloading robot: a six-axis KUKA arm with a suction gripper on a mobile base with an onboard conveyor, driven by the Dill Autonomy Engine. Unloads 400-1,500 cases per hour and is deployed at UPS.
Turnkey autonomous piece-picking system: a hybrid suction-and-finger gripper on UR5e/UR10e arms with ML vision. Picks up to 1,200 units per hour.

Medical robotic arm built for clinical use rather than adapted from an industrial robot. Kinova targets endoscopy, bronchoscopy and surgical interventions with it. Kinova launched it in 2026 for its 20th anniversary. It sits in the 3 kg payload class and has a frame under 13 kg. Every joint has redundant torque sensors. It has no separate control box: control runs over EtherCAT through a control library. Its software is IEC 62304 Class C.

Kinova calls Link 6 Canada's first industrial collaborative robot. Its controller has room for an optional GPU. It offers visual programming, manual guidance, a multi-purpose wrist with a coloured status ring, and native support for several industrial grippers. It launched in March 2022 and was available at launch.

Very small six-axis industrial arm with its controller built into the base. It has 5 µm repeatability and a 500 g rated payload; the manufacturer gives 1 kg as the maximum under certain conditions. Reach is 330 mm from the flange. It is used for micro-assembly, testing, inspection and dispensing. It was shown publicly in May 2015 and has been sold since July 2016. The current revision is Meca500-R4.

Compact micro-SCARA robot with its controller in the base and an optional smart vacuum and I/O module. It has 5 µm repeatability, a 225 mm reach and a 500 g rated payload (1 kg maximum under certain conditions). It can be mounted on a table or hung overhead. Pre-orders opened in 2023 after an early-access programme.

LARA (Lightweight Agile Robotic Assistant) is NEURA's 6-axis collaborative arm family, launched in November 2020. It runs from LARA 3 (3 kg payload, 590 mm reach) to LARA 30L (30 kg, 1800 mm). The maker states ±0.02 mm precision and 24/7 operation.

MAiRA is a 7-DOF 'cognitive' collaborative arm launched in 2021, with built-in 3D vision, voice recognition and force-torque sensing. It comes as MAiRA S (15-18 kg payload, 1100 mm reach, 51 kg), MAiRA M (12-14 kg, 1400 mm, 53 kg) and MAiRA L (9-11 kg, 1600 mm, 56 kg).

Franka Research 3 (FR3) is a 7-DOF force-sensitive arm for robotics and AI research. It succeeds the Panda and is made by Munich-based Franka Robotics, part of Agile Robots since 2023. It has a 3 kg payload, 855 mm reach, torque sensors in all seven joints and better than ±0.1 mm repeatability.
Franka Research 3 Duo is a dual-arm research setup built from FR3 arms. Franka Robotics showed it as a prototype at Automatica 2025, alongside a mobile version (Mobile FR3 Duo).

The KR810 is Kassow Robots' compact 7-axis collaborative arm, with a 10 kg payload and 850 mm reach. It supports ROS/ROS2 and Profinet. Kassow is based in Copenhagen and majority-owned by Bosch Rexroth.
The KR1205 is a 7-axis collaborative arm from Kassow Robots with a 5 kg payload and 1200 mm reach. It supports ROS/ROS2 and Profinet.
The KR1410 is a 7-axis collaborative arm from Kassow Robots with a 10 kg payload and 1400 mm reach.
The KR1805 is Kassow Robots' long-reach 7-axis collaborative arm, with a 5 kg payload and 1800 mm reach.

DEX-EE is a rugged three-fingered robot hand with 12 DOF that Shadow Robot built with Google DeepMind for real-world machine-learning research. Shadow unveiled it on 9 May 2024 as 'the world's most robust dexterous robot hand'. A chiral variant, DEX-EE Chiral, came later.

Bionic dexterous hand for humanoid robots. It has 6 coreless motors, 6 active joints and 11 DoF, multimodal tactile sensing, 50 N grip force, 0.1 mm precision and a 64 V wide input range. Basic and Haptic versions are sold.

Seven-axis medical cobot certified for integration into medical products (IEC 60601-1, IEC 62304). It has torque sensing in every axis and is rated IP54. It is used for surgical assistance, diagnostics and radiotherapy.
Higher-payload version of KUKA's medical-certified seven-axis LBR Med cobot, with 820 mm reach, safe torque measurement in every axis and an IP54 rating.
Six-axis, 5 kg cobot (Racer-5-0.80 COBOT) with 809 mm reach and 0.03 mm repeatability. It runs at industrial speed and drops to a 500 mm/s collaborative speed when LiDAR detects a person.
Smallest arm in Comau's six-model MyCo cobot family, with 3 kg payload, 590 mm reach and ±0.02 mm repeatability.
MyCo family cobot with 3.5 kg payload, 950 mm reach and ±0.02 mm repeatability.
MyCo family cobot with 5 kg payload, 800 mm reach and ±0.03 mm repeatability.
MyCo family cobot with 8 kg payload, 1300 mm reach and ±0.03 mm repeatability.
MyCo family cobot with 10 kg payload, 1000 mm reach and ±0.03 mm repeatability.

JetArm is a ROS 1/ROS 2 desktop robotic arm from Hiwonder for AI education that pairs a 3D vision camera with NVIDIA Jetson control. It supports multimodal large AI models for voice interaction and vision-guided recognition, sorting and grasping.

NexArm is an open-source ESP32 and AT32-based AI robotic arm platform from Hiwonder for embodied-AI and vision-language-action (VLA) learning. It uses magnetic-encoder bus servos with all-metal gears, supports a leader-follower teleoperation setup compatible with Hugging Face LeRobot for data collection, and adds AI vision and multimodal LLM interaction.

JetCobot is a 7-axis visual collaborative robotic arm from Yahboom controlled by an NVIDIA Jetson board, with a UR-like configuration and a maximum effective reach of 270 mm. A 0.3 MP 110° USB camera enables OpenCV-based color interaction, face tracking and tag recognition, and it supports ROS MoveIt simulation, gamepad and PC web control.

DOFBOT Pro is a desktop 6-DOF robotic arm from Yahboom for AI education that combines a 3D depth camera with an NVIDIA Jetson board (Nano 4GB, Orin Nano Super or Orin NX Super). It integrates large language models for voice-commanded, vision-guided recognition and grasping.

DOFBOT Ultra is a desktop AI robotic arm from Yahboom built on Raspberry Pi 5 or D-Robotics RDK X5 with 3D depth vision and large-language-model integration. Yahboom supplies tutorials covering assembly, motion control, Python, ROS 2, MoveIt and AI computer vision for education and research.

myBuddy 280 is Elephant Robotics' first dual-arm robot, a 13-axis humanoid-style collaborative robot powered by Raspberry Pi. Each arm has a 280 mm working radius, up to 250 g payload and 0.5 mm repeatability, and open control interfaces support research on dual-arm motion and object, face and image recognition. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 1699 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

mechArm 270 Pi is a compact six-axis desktop robotic arm from Elephant Robotics with an integrated Raspberry Pi 4B and a 270 mm radius of motion. It can be operated with an HDMI screen without a separate computer and offers open interfaces for object, face and image recognition projects; an M5Stack version is also sold. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 799 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

myPalletizer 260 is a compact four-axis desktop robotic arm from Elephant Robotics with a 260 mm radius of motion, sold in M5Stack and Raspberry Pi versions. It targets education and makers, supporting graphical programming and mainstream programming languages for palletizing and pick-and-place exercises. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 549 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

ultraArm P340 is a compact four-axis desktop robotic arm from Elephant Robotics with industrial-grade stepper motors and an all-metal body for AI vision, STEM education and light automation. It has a 340 mm reach and 650 g payload, and optional kits add laser engraving and drawing. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 999 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

myArm M750 is a 6-DOF robotic arm from Elephant Robotics with a 750 mm reach, 500 g rated payload (1 kg maximum) and a 1-DOF parallel gripper, aimed at embodied-AI research and household manipulation tasks. It can be paired with the myArm C650 motion-capture arm as a teleoperation and data-collection kit. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 1999 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

RoArm-M3-S is a 5+1-DOF ESP32-based desktop robotic arm from Waveshare with a 360° rotating base, a 2-DOF wrist and a workspace up to 1 m in diameter, carrying 200 g at 0.5 m. It supports web-app wireless control, inverse kinematics, ROS 2 and the LeRobot framework; the RoArm-M3-Pro variant uses all-metal ST3235 servos.

reBot Arm B601-DM is a fully open-source 6-axis robotic arm with a parallel gripper from Seeed Studio, built around Damiao actuators for embodied-AI learning and teleoperation. It offers up to 767 mm reach with the gripper, a 1.5 kg payload and repeatability under 0.2 mm, and Seeed publishes its BOM, drawings, software and algorithms.

Haro380 is a six-axis industrial mini robotic arm from WLKATA Robotics with harmonic reducers, a 380 mm reach, 500 g maximum payload and ±0.05 mm repeatability. It targets education, engineering projects and light manufacturing and was launched through crowdfunding in 2023.

MG400 is a lightweight four-axis desktop robotic arm from Dobot that fits in a 190 x 190 mm footprint, with a 750 g maximum payload and 440 mm maximum reach. It achieves ±0.05 mm repeatability, offers drag-to-teach and collision detection, and is programmed in Lua or a graphical interface for small-batch automation and lab work.

model: Robot Arm Kit for Raspberry Pi (FNK0036)
description: Freenove Robot Arm Kit is a metal-structure, stepper-motor robotic arm kit for Raspberry Pi (not included) with clamping and drawing modes and record-and-replay. It is controlled by app and comes with open-source code and tutorials.

myPalletizer 260 Pi is a compact 4-axis desktop robotic arm from Elephant Robotics with an embedded Raspberry Pi 4B and a 260 mm motion radius. It supports Blockly graphical programming and the my-series end-effector accessories. Elephant's online shop listed it at USD 649 in November 2026; regional prices, taxes and bundles differ.

Seven-axis force-controlled arm from Dobot (Shenzhen Yuejiang) aimed at wheeled dual-arm platforms, industrial mobile manipulation and embodied-AI development. It has torque sensors in every joint, a 7 kg rated payload, 725 mm reach, ±0.03 mm repeatability, IP54 protection and a stated 50,000-hour MTBF; it was launched at the China International Industry Fair on 12 October 2026.

Heavy-payload collaborative robot from Dobot, unveiled in Nagoya in June 2025, with Touch and Food (clean) editions. It carries a 30 kg rated payload over 1,800 mm reach with ±0.05 mm repeatability, weighs 100 kg, reaches up to 6 m/s TCP speed and is rated IP65/IP67.

Compact 6-axis collaborative robot from Dobot's Nova series, launched in November 2022 for retail and service tasks such as coffee and food preparation. It weighs 11 kg, carries 2 kg over a 625 mm working radius with ±0.05 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.

6-axis collaborative robot from Dobot's Nova series, launched in November 2022 for retail, food-service and physiotherapy applications. It weighs 14 kg, carries 5 kg over an 850 mm working radius with ±0.05 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.

Second-generation collaborative SCARA robot from Dobot, unveiled at iREX 2022, for pick-and-place, gluing and assembly in light industry and education. It weighs 15.7 kg, carries up to 1.5 kg over a 400 mm working radius with ±0.02 mm repeatability and has an integrated controller.

Six-axis desktop collaborative arm from Dobot for robotics education and research, presented as newly released at Automate 2024. It weighs up to 7.2 kg, carries 750 g over a 450 mm working radius with ±0.1 mm repeatability and runs on 48 V DC.

Largest model of Dobot's CRA collaborative robot series launched in 2023. It weighs 73 kg, carries 20 kg over a 1,700 mm working radius with ±0.05 mm repeatability, reaches 2 m/s TCP speed and is rated IP54.
Smallest model of Dobot's CRA collaborative robot series introduced in 2023. It weighs 16.5 kg, carries 3 kg over a 620 mm working radius with ±0.02 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.
10 kg model of Dobot's CRA collaborative robot series introduced in 2023. It weighs 40 kg, carries 10 kg over a 1,300 mm working radius with ±0.03 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.

Large-payload flexible collaborative robot in ROKAE's xMate CR35 series, launched in September 2025 for palletizing and heavy handling. It carries 35 kg over a 2,246 mm reach with ±0.05 mm repeatability, weighs about 180 kg and has an IP67-rated body.

Highest-payload variant of ROKAE's xMate CR35 flexible collaborative robot series launched in September 2025. It carries 45 kg over a 1,947 mm reach with ±0.05 mm repeatability, weighs about 175 kg and has an IP67-rated body.

Long-reach variant of ROKAE's NB12 series of six-axis industrial robots, launched in February 2023 as an upgrade of the XB series. It carries 10 kg over a 1,602 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability, weighs about 117 kg and has an IP67 body.

Higher-payload variant of ROKAE's NB12 series of six-axis industrial robots launched in February 2023. It carries 16 kg over a 1,102 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability, weighs about 112 kg and has an IP67 body.

Lightweight 7-DoF humanoid force-controlled arm from ROKAE with joint torque sensors and a cross-axis wrist, launched in March 2026 for service humanoids and embodied-AI platforms. It weighs 8 kg, carries 3 kg over a 650 mm radius with ±0.05 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.

Heavy-duty 7-DoF humanoid force-controlled arm from ROKAE, launched in March 2026 for load handling and assembly on industrial humanoid and dual-arm platforms. It weighs 19.5 kg, carries 10 kg over an 815 mm radius with ±0.1 mm repeatability and is rated IP54.

Six-axis 3 kg collaborative robot from FAIRINO (Fairino (Suzhou) Robot Technology), introduced with a 22,800 CNY guide price in March 2023. It has a 622 mm reach, ±0.02 mm repeatability, weighs about 15 kg without cable and is rated IP54 (IP65 optional).

Six-axis 5 kg collaborative robot from FAIRINO, introduced with a 23,800 CNY guide price in March 2023 and widely used for welding, handling and machine tending. It has a 922 mm reach, ±0.02 mm repeatability, weighs about 22 kg and is rated IP54 (IP65 optional).

Six-axis heavy-payload collaborative robot from FAIRINO, launched at the company's March 2024 product event for palletizing, handling and high-torque tasks. It carries 30 kg (35 kg maximum) over a 1,403 mm reach with ±0.1 mm repeatability, weighs about 85 kg and is rated IP54 (IP65 optional).

Seven-axis industrial humanoid force-controlled arm from FAIRINO with full-joint force control and a crossed wrist, first shown at the World Robot Conference in August 2026 and also offered as the ART7-R7 dual-arm torso. It carries 7 kg (10 kg peak) over a 714 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability and runs on 48 V DC.

Heavy-duty industrial humanoid force-controlled arm in FAIRINO's ART series, first shown at the World Robot Conference in August 2026 for automotive manufacturing, large-part handling and assembly. It carries 14 kg per arm with a 20 kg peak payload.

High-payload collaborative robot from JAKA, premiered at the China International Industry Fair in October 2026 to extend the Zu series into heavy handling and palletizing. It carries 50 kg over a 2,100 mm reach with ±0.05 mm repeatability, weighs 160 kg and is rated IP65.

Collaborative robot from JAKA's Zu series for large workpieces, handling, welding, gluing and palletizing, premiered at Hannover Messe in April 2024. It carries 20 kg over a 1,780 mm reach with ±0.05 mm repeatability, weighs 68 kg including cables and is rated IP65.

Lightweight six-axis collaborative robot from JAKA, launched at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on 7 July 2021 for commercial, retail and education uses. It carries 1 kg over a 580 mm reach with ±0.1 mm repeatability, weighs 9.4 kg including cables and runs on 24 V DC.

20 kg collaborative robot added to Elite Robots' CS series in 2023 and introduced at EASTEC in May 2023 for palletizing and welding. It has an 1,800 mm reach, ±0.1 mm repeatability, a dual 3 A/5 A tool connector, weighs 60 kg and is rated IP65 (IP68 optional).

Desktop six-axis arm from RealMan (Beijing) launched in October 2026 at a roughly 10,000 CNY price level for light automation, mobile manipulation, embodied-AI data collection and teaching. It weighs 3.5 kg, has a 2 kg rated payload (3.5 kg maximum at full reach), a 660 mm working radius, ±0.1 mm repeatability, all-harmonic drives and runs on 24 V DC.

Ultra-compact embedded six-axis arm from RealMan with a base-integrated controller, released on 15 October 2026 under the 'Arm in Machine' concept for installation inside coffee stations, vending terminals and other equipment. It weighs 3.6 kg, carries 2 kg over a 425 mm working radius with ±0.1 mm repeatability and draws under 100 W typical at 24 V.

Compact six-axis collaborative arm from Elephant Robotics introduced in August 2025 with harmonic joint modules, joint brakes and integrated controllers for education, research and light industrial use. It carries 1 kg over a 450 mm working radius with ±0.1 mm repeatability and supports Python, C++, ROS and integration with large language models. Elephant publishes no global price; regional prices and bundles differ.

Four-axis desktop stepper-motor arm from Elephant Robotics launched in July 2026 as an upgrade of the ultraArm P340, aimed at education, research and light palletizing. It carries 650 g over a 360 mm working radius with ±0.1 mm repeatability, has collision detection and a 2.4-inch screen, and accepts pen, gripper, suction and laser-engraving tools. Elephant publishes no global price; regional prices and bundles differ.

Three-axis force-controlled parallel (delta-type) robot from Flexiv, announced on 31 January 2023 as the company's first adaptive parallel robot. It weighs 38 kg, carries 7 kg (12 kg maximum) over a 1,200 mm diameter x 400 mm high workspace with ±0.05 mm repeatability, can be mounted at any angle and is rated IP65.

New-generation lightweight adaptive robot arm series from Flexiv, launched at the FLEXIVERSE 2026 event in Shanghai on 20 March 2026 together with the Orion controller and MICO dual-arm platform. Every joint integrates multi-axis force sensing for whole-body skin-level contact perception, detecting up to seven simultaneous contact points with millimetre-level position and 0.5 N-level touch-force sensitivity.

Seven-axis humanoid arm in the Echo series from Huayan Robotics (formerly Han's Robot), launched in April 2026 for quadruped, humanoid and other embodied platforms. It has a coplanar crossed wrist, joint torque sensing in every joint, a 5 kg rated payload (6 kg peak), 735 mm maximum reach, ±0.03 mm repeatability, EtherCAT control at 48 V DC and native ROS 2 support.

Seven-axis humanoid arm in the Echo series from Huayan Robotics (formerly Han's Robot), launched in April 2026 for quadruped, humanoid and other embodied platforms. It has a coplanar crossed wrist, joint torque sensing in every joint, a 15 kg rated payload (16 kg peak), 854 mm maximum reach, ±0.05 mm repeatability, EtherCAT control at 48 V DC and native ROS 2 support.

Seven-axis humanoid arm in the HY series from Huayan Robotics (formerly Han's Robot), launched in April 2026 for quadruped, humanoid and other embodied platforms. It has a non-coplanar crossed wrist, joint torque sensing in every joint, a 3.5 kg rated payload (4.5 kg peak), 650 mm maximum reach, ±0.02 mm repeatability, EtherCAT control at 48 V DC and native ROS 2 support.

Seven-axis humanoid arm in the HY series from Huayan Robotics (formerly Han's Robot), launched in April 2026 for quadruped, humanoid and other embodied platforms. It has a non-coplanar crossed wrist, joint torque sensing in every joint, a 7 kg rated payload (8 kg peak), 670 mm maximum reach, ±0.03 mm repeatability, EtherCAT control at 48 V DC and native ROS 2 support.

Five-axis 60 kg large-payload collaborative robot in the S series of Huayan Robotics (formerly Han's Robot), launched in 2025 for palletizing, heavy handling and machine loading. It reaches 2,000 mm with ±0.1 mm repeatability, weighs 151 kg, reaches 6.4 m/s tool speed and is rated IP54.

35 kg large-payload collaborative robot in the iS series from AUBO (Beijing) Intelligent Technology, introduced in 2025. It has six axes, a 2,100 mm working radius, ±0.05 mm repeatability, up to 4 m/s tool speed, weighs 172 kg and is rated IP54 (IP67 on request).

Desktop dual-arm embodied-AI development platform from Galaxea (Xinghaitu), put on sale in October 2026 at a 49,999 CNY launch price. It combines two A1Z arms (14 DoF in total) with G1Z grippers, two wrist cameras and a top camera and a CCU controller, offering 3 kg rated / 5 kg peak payload per arm, ±0.1 mm repeatability, isomorphic leader-follower teleoperation and synchronized multimodal data collection.

ROS 2 desktop robot arm from Hiwonder with an all-metal aluminium frame, intelligent bus servos and a monocular or depth camera, listed in 2025. It supports 3D vision grasping and multimodal large-language-model voice interaction; the standard kit weighs 1.47 kg and measures 288 x 177 x 450 mm.

Desktop programmable robot arm from Hiwonder with 5 DOF plus gripper, smart serial bus servos and an ESP32-based CoreX controller, listed in 2025 with AI vision and voice interaction. It weighs 1.28 kg and measures 293 x 153 x 426 mm.

Baxter is a two-armed collaborative manufacturing robot unveiled by Rethink Robotics in 2012, with series elastic actuators for force sensing, five cameras, a head sonar array and an LCD face, and programming by demonstration. Each arm has 7 degrees of freedom; the robot was discontinued after Rethink Robotics shut down in 2018.

Quattro is a four-arm parallel (delta-type) pick-and-place robot originally designed by Adept Technology in 2006 and now sold by Omron, capable of more than 300 picks per minute. It handles payloads up to 15 kg with a 1,600 mm XY stroke and 500 mm Z stroke, and hygienic versions are offered for primary and secondary food handling.

Unimate was the first industrial robot, a hydraulic manipulator built by Unimation of Danbury, Connecticut and put into service in 1961 at a General Motors plant to unload hot metal parts from a die-casting machine. It stored hundreds of programmed steps on a magnetic drum memory, offered position repeatability within 1 mm and sold for about 35,000 USD in the early 1970s.

Jaco is a lightweight carbon-fiber robotic arm from Kinova of Canada, introduced in 2009, with a 6-DoF arm and 3-finger underactuated gripper. It was designed to be mounted on power wheelchairs to help people with upper-body disabilities eat, drink and open doors, and a research version with ROS interfaces sold for about 50,000 USD.

Promobot M13 is a six-axis collaborative robot arm made by Russian robotics company Promobot for industrial automation. It carries a 13 kg payload with a working radius of up to 1,300 mm and IP54 protection; Promobot started series production in May 2024.

Promobot M Edu is a four-axis desktop educational robot arm from Russian maker Promobot, announced in July 2024 for teaching robotics, automation and programming (Python, C/C++) in schools and universities. Interchangeable tool modules cover gripping, vacuum pick-up, laser engraving, 3D printing and drawing.

7-axis humanoid-style robotic arm from Topstar's embodied-intelligence line, launched alongside its first humanoid in 2025. It has a 690 mm working radius, 5 kg rated (10 kg max) payload, 15 kg body weight without controller, ±0.03 mm repeatability and EtherCAT communication.

Tabletop leader-follower teleoperation station from ARX Robotics with two X5 follower arms, two compact teaching arms and three cameras for recording two-arm demonstrations for VLA model training. Each follower arm has six joints plus a gripper, about 500 g payload, about 1 mm repeatability and a 200 Hz control loop; list price is 6,999 USD after a 5,999 USD launch offer.

Lightweight force-controlled 6-DOF arm with gripper from ARX Robotics (方舟无限), launched in October 2023 and built with quasi-direct-drive motors. It is used in many embodied-AI research setups and is programmed through ARX's Python SDK over CAN at 200 Hz.

6-DOF position- and force-controlled arm from ARX Robotics launched in July 2024 for embodied-AI research, with VR teleoperation support, force feedback and collision detection. It has a 620 mm working radius, 500 W rated power and runs on Ubuntu.

Higher-payload version of the ARX L5 force-controlled research arm, launched in July 2024 with a 3 kg rated payload (double the L5) and the same 620 mm working radius, VR teleoperation support and collision detection.

Desktop dual-arm teleoperation and multimodal data-collection platform from AgileX Robotics built around two 7-DOF NERO arms (3 kg payload, 580 mm reach and ±0.1 mm repeatability per arm) with grippers opening 0-100 mm and an Intel i5 onboard PC. It records data in MCAP and LeRobot formats for robot-learning research.

Lightweight desktop dual-arm teleoperation platform from AgileX Robotics using 6-DOF PiPER arms, aimed at bimanual manipulation, teleoperation data collection and embodied-AI prototyping with standardized components and rapid assembly.
7-DOF humanoid-style robot arm from AgileX Robotics for embodied-AI and manipulation research, with 3 kg payload, 580 mm reach, ±0.1 mm repeatability, 24 V DC supply and CAN interface.
Lightweight 6-DOF robot arm from AgileX Robotics used in its COBOT MAGIC and other teleoperation platforms, with 1.5 kg payload, 626 mm reach, ±0.1 mm repeatability and a CAN interface.
Version of the AgileX PiPER 6-DOF arm with a spherical wrist for manipulation in constrained spaces, offering 1.5 kg payload, 669 mm reach and ±0.1 mm repeatability; listed by AgileX in January 2026.

7-DOF research arm from DISCOVER Robotics launched on 23 July 2026 with a built-in D-Robotics Sunrise 5 chip (10 TOPS) and an 8-core Cortex-A55 processor for on-arm policy inference. It offers 3 kg payload, 640 mm reach, ±0.1 mm repeatability, brakes on every joint, gravity-compensated hand guiding and ROS 2, Python and C++ interfaces.

Dual-arm robot 'Lingke' from Shanghai Electric, presented in 2025 as a product of its 'Peiyuan' industrial embodied-skill training ground. Its modular design allows quick changes between grinding and flaw-detection tools, and high-precision force control with intelligent path planning lets it work on local areas of large components at more than five times manual efficiency.

Open-source Jetson Nano robot arm from Hiwonder made of metal and carbon fibre with 4+1 DOF and serial bus servos, listed in 2022. It carries 450 g and supports ROS, vision recognition and Python programming.

Raspberry Pi-powered vision robot arm from Hiwonder with 4 DOF plus gripper, a 170-degree wide-angle camera and OpenCV-based colour recognition, sorting, tracking and palletizing, listed in 2022. It weighs 0.7 kg and measures 208 x 134 x 309 mm.

Six-axis desktop industrial-grade robot arm from WLKATA Robotics listed in July 2026 for automation teaching and CTE workcells. It has a 1 kg rated payload, 450 mm reach and ±0.05 mm repeatability, quick-change tools and Blockly, Python, ROS, MATLAB, C++ and Modbus control.

Metal four-axis (4+1 DoF) desktop robot arm from WLKATA Robotics listed in 2024 for labs and STEM teaching. It carries 500 g (600 g maximum) with 0.1 mm repeatability and offers USB/serial, RS485, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi control with ROS 2 and Arduino support.

Adaptive heavy-payload collaborative robot in AUBO's G series, released on 30 April 2026, with torque sensors in every joint and a 96 V high-voltage power platform. It carries 42 kg over a 1,800 mm working radius with ±0.05 mm repeatability, reaches up to 5.4 m/s tool speed, weighs 109 kg and is rated IP67.

Robot Kol 4.2 is a domestically-produced industrial robotic arm by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS, fitted with an 85mm-opening gripper and rated to carry and place objects up to 5kg for pick-and-place and material-handling tasks.

ReBeL is a lightweight collaborative robot arm made largely of igus own lubrication-free motion plastics, sold by the German motion-plastics company igus through its RBTX low-cost automation marketplace. It is offered in 4-axis and 6-axis versions with payload up to 2 kg and reach up to 600 mm, aimed at pick-and-place, packaging, quality inspection and other low-cost automation tasks, and can be combined with a 7th-axis linear transfer unit.

size: 100 x 60 x 80 cm (closed) / 100 x 60 x 110 cm (open)
description: flowbot ONE is a benchtop liquid-handling robot from Danish company Flow Robotics that automates pipetting for laboratories without requiring coding, using a browser-based drag-and-drop interface and an open API. It has a 12-position deck and supports 1-, 4- and 8-channel pipettes covering 1-20uL, 2-200uL and 10-1000uL volume ranges, and is used for applications such as PCR/qPCR setup, ELISA, cell culture and sample normalization.

LINQ Bench is a configurable, modular lab-automation hardware platform from UK robotics company Automata, combining robotic arms, a vertical rack storage system and plate-transport modules (including a MagLev high-throughput transport system) that can be arranged in linear, island or corner layouts. It is the hardware half of Automata's LINQ lab-automation platform, which pairs it with cloud software and a Python SDK for building and running automated lab workflows, and it won a Red Dot Design Award in 2025.

The Taibai AR5 is a 7-DOF anthropomorphic force-control robotic arm from ROKAE (Beijing), part of the AR series alongside the AR3 and AR10. It weighs 10kg, has a 700mm reach, joint-level torque sensing, and is aimed at data collection, AI training and smart-factory tasks.

MOTOMAN-NEX20 is a 20 kg payload industrial robot arm from Yaskawa Motoman, part of the NEX series of AI-enabled "adaptive, intelligent" robots launched under the MOTOMAN NEXT physical-AI initiative shown at iREX 2025. It has a 1552 mm horizontal reach and 2699 mm vertical reach and is aimed at assembly and material-handling tasks using perception-guided autonomy.

MOTOMAN-HC20DTP is a 6-axis collaborative robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's HC series, rated for a 20 kg payload with a 1700 mm horizontal reach and 3400 mm vertical reach. It is designed to work directly alongside people on assembly and handling lines without safety fencing.

The AX6 is Seiko Epson's first collaborative 6-axis industrial robot arm, unveiled in September 2026 and launched for sale in Japan in November 2026. It has a 900 mm reach, supports Python programming alongside no-code teaching, and is aimed at manufacturers wanting a cobot that works safely alongside people without full specialist programming expertise.

COBOTTA PRO 1300 is a 6-axis collaborative robot arm from DENSO WAVE with a 1,300 mm arm length, 1,463 mm reach, 12 kg maximum payload and torque sensors on every axis for safe human collaboration. It reaches 2,500 mm/s when no worker is nearby, is IP54 rated with ISO Class 5 cleanroom capability, and supports Blockly-based visual programming plus Mech-Eye 3D camera integration.

The MZS05 is Nachi-Fujikoshi's small-payload collaborative robot arm, with a 927 mm reach, 6 axes and a repeatability of ±0.020 mm. It automatically slows or stops for operator safety and is used for tasks such as parts sorting.

The MELFA RV-12CRL is a vertically articulated 6-axis industrial robot arm launched by Mitsubishi Electric in October 2024, with a 12 kg payload and 1,504 mm reach. It uses MELSERVO-J5 servo motors with no encoder batteries and the CR800 controller, and is positioned as an affordable industrial-grade arm for machine tending, case packing and pick-and-place tasks.

HORST600 G2 is the most compact 6-axis cobot in fruitcore robotics' German-made HORST family, built for pick-and-place and parts handling with a 7 kg maximum payload (5 kg nominal per VDI 2861-2) and 610 mm reach. It ships with an integrated control unit and touchscreen running the no-code horstOS software, floor/wall/ceiling/incline mounting, and IP54/IP65 protection.

HORST1000 G2 is a German-made 6-axis cobot from fruitcore robotics billed as the strongest in its class, with a 16 kg payload and 1141 mm reach for machine-tending in harsh production environments. It integrates a control unit, touchscreen panel and the no-code horstOS automation software, with +/-0.05 mm repeatability.

HORST1500 G2 is the largest 6-axis cobot in fruitcore robotics' German-made HORST line, with a 15 kg payload and 1485 mm reach for loading/unloading machine tools and palletizing. It carries IP54/IP65 ratings and ISO 6 cleanroom capability, and runs the no-code horstOS software with +/-0.05 mm repeatability.

DR1000 is a delta robot from German manufacturer igus for high-speed pick-and-place, with a 1000 mm working diameter available in a 3-axis version (LCA-DR1000-03) and a 4-axis version with an added rotary axis (LCA-DR1000-04). It carries up to 2.5 kg at up to 2.0 m/s (28 m/s squared acceleration) for up to 111 picks per minute, and runs on the free igus Robot Control software.

WX143 is a pick-and-place robot in Austrian machine-builder Wittmann's W9/WX series for injection-molding part removal, with fixed or moving demolding axes, reinforced profiles, an integrated energy-storage system for about 20% energy savings, and the R9 touchscreen control with live 3D robot animation.

Primus 148T is a cost-efficient three-axis pick-and-place robot in Austrian machine-builder Wittmann's Primus series, built for injection-molding machines from 20-900 tons clamping force with a lightweight rib-reinforced aluminum vertical arm and the R9 Primus touchscreen control.

P-Rob Eco is a cost-efficient collaborative robot arm from Swiss manufacturer F&P Robotics for sample handling, light assembly, inspection and R&D automation in laboratories, research institutions and industry. It has force-limited joints and soft edges for safe human collaboration without safety cages.

Panda was Franka Emika's original 7-axis collaborative research robot arm, a widely adopted force-sensitive platform in robotics labs worldwide with a 3 kg payload. Franka Emika filed for insolvency in 2023 and was acquired by Agile Robots, which has succeeded Panda with the Franka Research 3 as the company's current research arm; Panda is no longer listed as a current product.

TX2-40 is the smallest 6-axis articulated robot in Swiss manufacturer Staubli's TX2 family, with a 515 mm reach, 2 kg payload and +/-0.02 mm repeatability. It uses the CS9 controller and supports modular safety up to SIL3/PL e for handling, machine tending, assembly and inspection tasks.

TX2-90 is a mid-range 6-axis articulated robot in Swiss manufacturer Staubli's TX2 family, with a 1000-1450 mm reach, 7-14 kg payload and +/-0.02 mm repeatability, paired with the CS9 controller for handling, assembly, inspection and packaging.

TX2-200 is the heavy-payload flagship of Swiss manufacturer Staubli's TX2 6-axis articulated robot family, with a 2209-2609 mm reach, 110-170 kg payload and +/-0.02 mm repeatability, running on the high-power CS9 HP controller for large-scale handling and assembly operations.

TS2-60 is a modular SCARA robot in Swiss manufacturer Staubli's TS2 family, with a 620 mm reach, 8.4 kg payload and +/-0.01 mm repeatability in a hygienic, encapsulated design for ultra-short-cycle-time assembly and pick-and-place automation.

The N-220 is a high-payload industrial robot in Comau's new-generation N-series, built on a modular architecture with compact motors and new control drivers at Comau's Turin Innovation Center. It has a 220 kg payload, a wide working envelope and Performance Level D cartesian safety, and is aimed at spot welding, material handling, 3D printing and gluing in automotive, food and beverage, and logistics applications.

Racer-7-1.4 is a six-axis general-industry robot from Italian automation maker Comau, part of the Racer line. It has a 7 kg wrist payload (10 kg additional forearm load), a 1436 mm maximum horizontal reach, 0.05 mm repeatability, IP54 protection and a 180 kg robot weight, and can be floor-, ceiling- or incline-mounted.

Niryo One was the first product from French robotics maker Niryo: an open-source, 6-axis desktop robotic arm aimed at makers, educators and developers, controllable through ROS. It was superseded by Niryo's later Ned and Ned2 arms and is no longer sold as the company's current lineup.

Krab is a dual-armed manipulation robot from Sber's Robotics Center that uses AI for automatic action planning and also supports teleoperated remote control for handling objects. It was unveiled alongside the Topa, Kuba and Slon robots at Sber's AI Journey 2024 conference.

Yamaha Motor Cobot is a 7-axis collaborative robot arm from Yamaha Motor's industrial robotics division, released alongside a compact dedicated DC48V controller. It is positioned in Yamaha's robot lineup alongside the company's SCARA, single-axis and Cartesian robot product lines for factory automation tasks that require close human-robot collaboration.

The YK1200XG is a large-type SCARA robot in Yamaha Motor's YK-XG series, launched with a dedicated RCX341 controller. Yamaha states it has a 1,200 mm arm length and a maximum payload of 50 kg, which the company markets as achieving industry-leading cycle times for its size class.

The GX20C is the largest-reach model in Epson Robots' GX-C series of SCARA robots, available with 850 mm or 1,000 mm arm reach options. It ships with Epson's RC800A controller featuring SafeSense safety technology and GYROPLUS vibration-reduction technology for faster settling times, and became available through Epson's distributor network in April 2025 alongside the smaller GX4C, GX8C and GX10C models.

The VT6L-DC is an all-in-one, 48VDC-powered six-axis robot arm from Epson Robots with a built-in controller housed in the robot base, a 6 kg payload and up to 900 mm reach. It is designed to be mounted on an AMR or other mobile platform so it can move between workstations in a warehouse, and supports both the traditional Epson RC+ programming environment and the no-code RC+ Express interface. It launched in October 2022.

COBOTTA is DENSO Wave's original compact desktop collaborative robot, a 6-axis arm plus a 1-axis electric gripper unit with a 342.5 mm combined arm length, about 4 kg total weight and a 0.5 kg rated payload (0.7 kg with the wrist angled 10 degrees downward). It was developed for small-parts assembly and inspection tasks on desktops and in confined spaces and predates the larger, faster COBOTTA PRO line introduced in 2021.

The SR-6iA is a SCARA robot in FANUC's small-robot lineup, with a 6 kg payload, 650 mm reach and 210 mm vertical stroke, powered by the R-30iB Compact Plus controller. It was introduced alongside the smaller SR-3iA (3 kg payload, 400 mm reach) for high-speed pick-and-place, assembly, testing and inspection tasks.

The MOTOMAN-HC10DTP is a six-axis collaborative robot arm from Yaskawa with a 10 kg payload, 1,379 mm maximum reach (1,200 mm effective reach) and +/-0.05 mm repeatability. It uses power-and-force-limiting technology to monitor contact forces and can switch between a safety-rated collaborative speed mode and full industrial speed, running on Yaskawa's YRC1000 controller for assembly, dispensing, machine tending, material handling, packaging and welding tasks. It launched alongside the larger HC20DTP in February 2022.

The P3020 is a collaborative robot arm from Doosan Robotics' Prime (P) series, launched in 2024 with what the maker calls the industry's best combination of payload and reach for palletizing. It is built for heavy-duty logistics and material-handling tasks and is sold across Europe, including the UK and Nordic region, via Doosan's distributor network.

The H2017 is a high-payload cobot in Doosan Robotics' High-Power (H) series, using six torque sensors across its axes for precise, safe heavy-duty work. It targets metalworking, logistics, machine-tending and palletizing applications and is sold through Doosan distributors in Europe.

The M1509 is the flagship model of Doosan Robotics' Masterpiece (M) series, using six high-performance torque sensors per axis for precision work and what the maker describes as industry-leading safety. It is aimed at electronics and automotive machine-tending and assembly tasks and is sold via Doosan's European distributor network.

The A0509 is a compact cobot in Doosan Robotics' Agile (A) series, positioned for high speed and economic efficiency in general-purpose industrial automation. It is used in food-and-beverage and healthcare settings for tasks such as inspection and adhesive application, and is distributed throughout Europe.

The E0509 is Doosan Robotics' Edge (E) series cobot built specifically for the food-and-beverage industry, with NSF certification and an IP66 rating for washdown and hygienic maintenance. It performs tasks such as inspection and gluing/bonding in food production and medical settings.

PoWa 10 is part of ABB Robotics' PoWa cobot family launched in April 2026, built for long reach and high arm-load capacity in compact industrial spaces. It reaches top speeds of 5.8 m/s and runs on ABB's OmniCore controller with no-code programming via RobotStudio and Wizard Easy Programming, targeting machine tending, palletizing, screwdriving and arc welding.

PoWa 13 is part of ABB Robotics' PoWa cobot family launched in April 2026, one of six payload variants (7-30 kg) built for long reach and high arm-load capacity in compact industrial spaces. It reaches top speeds of 5.8 m/s and runs on ABB's OmniCore controller with no-code programming via RobotStudio and Wizard Easy Programming.

GRASS SR40 is a six-axis industrial robotic arm developed by Turkish company Altinay Robot Teknolojileri under the state-backed GRASS (Gelismis Akilli Sanayii Sistemleri) program, which designs and builds robot arms and their core components, including servo motors, drives and motion-control software, domestically in Turkey. It was publicly launched in May 2026 at the Istanbul Fair Center with Turkey's defence and technology ministers in attendance, and carries a 40 kg nominal (50 kg maximum) payload with a 2100 mm reach for manufacturing and heavy-industry automation lines.

GRASS SR80 is the higher-capacity sibling of the GRASS SR40, a six-axis industrial robotic arm developed in Turkey by Altinay Robot Teknolojileri under the government-backed GRASS domestic-robotics program and launched in May 2026. It carries an 80 kg nominal (90 kg maximum) payload with a 2300 mm reach, aimed at heavier automation lines across defence, heavy industry and automotive manufacturing.

Canadarm, officially the Shuttle Remote Manipulator System, was a three-jointed robotic arm built for NASA's Space Shuttle program with Canadian industry led by MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates (now MDA Space). It could lift over 30,000 kg on Earth (up to 266,000 kg in microgravity) using less power than a kettle, and flew 90 missions deploying and retrieving satellites and assisting station assembly over 30 years before retiring after STS-135 in 2011.

Canadarm2 is a 17-metre robotic arm built by MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates (MDA Space) that has operated on the International Space Station since 2001, handling payloads up to 116,000 kg. It performs station maintenance, grapples and berths visiting cargo spacecraft, and transports astronauts, equipment and the Dextre robotic assistant along the station's exterior using identical Latching End Effectors at each end.

Dextre (the Special Purpose Dexterous Manipulator) is a twin-armed robotic handyman built by MacDonald, Dettwiler and Associates (MDA Space) and launched to the International Space Station in 2008, with each seven-jointed arm able to handle objects from toaster-sized components to 100 kg batteries with millimetre precision. Operated from Earth, it installs and replaces external equipment, swaps faulty electrical components and inspects the station for ammonia leaks, reducing the need for astronaut spacewalks.

Canadarm3 is MDA Space's next-generation robotic arm system for NASA's lunar Gateway station, publicly unveiled in 2019 as Canada's contribution to the Artemis program. It will comprise a large 8.5-metre arm, a smaller dexterous arm and a tool caddy, designed as a goal-driven autonomous system that can perform maintenance, assembly and astronaut-support tasks with minimal human intervention about 400,000 km from Earth. As of 2026 it remains in development, with delivery to Gateway not expected before 2029.

Mantis is FBR's robotic welding system for defence and heavy fabrication sectors such as mining, shipbuilding and large-scale industrial manufacturing, built on the company's Dynamic Stabilisation Technology for precise welding at a full 8-metre reach. It runs dual Fronius TPS 500i welders for high-deposition twin-wire welding up to 25 kg/hr, supports a pendulum workflow across up to four workspaces, and is programmed via AI Weld Creator or Verbotics; it completed factory acceptance testing in October 2026.

Firehawk is FBR's autonomous refractory ladle-relining robot for the steelmaking industry, built on the company's Dynamic Stabilisation Technology to place insulating sand and refractory brick with consistent accuracy across a 10-metre reach. It removes workers from extreme-heat, confined-space ladle environments, runs one-touch operation from pre-approved lining designs, and can complete a full reline in as little as a day.

The GP7 is a compact six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 7 kg payload with a 927 mm horizontal and 1,693 mm vertical reach. It runs on Yaskawa's YRC1000 or YRC1000micro controller and is marketed for high-speed assembly, handling, pick-and-place and dispensing tasks.

The GP8 is a compact, high-speed six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for an 8 kg payload with a 727 mm horizontal and 1,312 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 or YRC1000micro controller and is positioned for fast assembly, handling and pick-and-place work in a small footprint.

The GP12 is a six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 12 kg payload with a 1,440 mm horizontal and 2,511 mm vertical reach. Yaskawa markets it for high-transfer-capability applications such as material handling, part transfer and pick-and-pack, running on the YRC1000 or YRC1000micro controller.

The GP25 is a six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 25 kg payload with a 1,730 mm horizontal and 3,089 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 controller and is aimed at high-volume material handling, packaging and pick-and-place applications.

The GP35L is an extended-reach six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 35 kg payload with a 2,538 mm horizontal and 4,449 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 controller and is marketed for material handling, part transfer and press-tending applications.

The GP50 is a long-reach six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 50 kg payload with a 2,061 mm horizontal and 3,578 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 controller and is positioned for material handling, part transfer and press-tending applications needing extra reach.

The GP110 is a high-payload six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 110 kg payload with a 2,236 mm horizontal and 3,751 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 controller and is built for heavy part processing such as machine tending, deburring/trimming and material handling.

The GP225 is a heavy-payload six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's GP series, rated for a 225 kg payload with a 2,702 mm horizontal and 3,393 mm vertical reach. It runs on the YRC1000 controller and is engineered with high moment and inertia ratings for heavy part handling, part transfer and press tending.

MotoMini is a sub-compact six-axis industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's lineup, marketed as the smallest 6-axis robotic arm in the industry with a 0.5 kg payload, 350 mm horizontal and 495 mm vertical reach. It runs on the compact YRC1000micro controller with internal cabling and is aimed at small-parts assembly, pick-and-pack and pick-and-place tasks requiring high acceleration in a tight footprint.

The HC30PL is a 30 kg-payload collaborative robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's HC series, purpose-built for palletizing with a 1,700 mm horizontal and 3,400 mm vertical reach. It is IP65-67 rated, supports direct hand-guided teaching, uses power-and-force-limiting technology for fenceless operation, and runs on the YRC1000 or YRC1000micro controller.

The NHC10 is a 10 kg-payload six-axis robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's newer N-series lineup, with a 1,000 mm horizontal and 600 mm vertical reach, built for material-handling tasks. It runs on Yaskawa's newer YNX1000 controller.

The NEX7 is a 7.0 kg-payload industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's NEX series of AI-enabled 'adaptive, intelligent' robots shown at iREX 2025 under the MOTOMAN NEXT physical-AI initiative. It has a 927 mm horizontal and 1693 mm vertical reach, runs on the YNX1000 controller with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin-based Autonomous Control Unit, and is rated IP67 for assembly, material handling and pick-and-pack tasks in electronics, food and medical settings.

The NEX10 is a 10 kg-payload industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's NEX series of AI-enabled 'adaptive, intelligent' robots shown at iREX 2025 under the MOTOMAN NEXT physical-AI initiative. It has a 1101 mm horizontal and 2027 mm vertical reach, runs on the YNX1000 controller with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin-based Autonomous Control Unit, and is rated IP67 for assembly, material handling and pick-and-pack tasks in electronics, food and medical settings.

The NEX35 is a 35 kg-payload industrial robot arm in Yaskawa Motoman's NEX series of AI-enabled 'adaptive, intelligent' robots shown at iREX 2025 under the MOTOMAN NEXT physical-AI initiative. It has a 2063 mm horizontal and 3715 mm vertical reach, runs on the YNX1000 controller with an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin-based Autonomous Control Unit, and is rated IP67 for assembly, material handling and pick-and-pack tasks in electronics, food and medical settings.

The GX1C is the smallest model in Epson Robots' GX-C SCARA lineup, a 4-axis arm rated for 0.5 kg (1 kg maximum) payload offered with 175 mm or 225 mm arm reach. It runs on Epson's RC800A controller with SafeSense technology and GYROPLUS vibration-reduction, aimed at small-parts assembly and pick-and-place work.

The GX4C is a 4-axis SCARA robot in Epson Robots' GX-C series, launched in April 2025 alongside the GX8C, GX10C and GX20C, with a 2 kg rated (4 kg maximum) payload and 250, 300 or 350 mm arm-length options. It runs on Epson's RC800A controller with SafeSense safety technology and GYROPLUS vibration reduction for fast settling times.

The GX8C is a 4-axis SCARA robot in Epson Robots' GX-C series, launched in April 2025 alongside the GX4C, GX10C and GX20C, with a 4 kg rated (8 kg maximum) payload and 450, 550 or 650 mm arm-length options. It runs on Epson's RC800A controller with SafeSense safety technology, and IP65-protected models are offered alongside standard and ISO Class 3 cleanroom variants.

The LS8C is a 4-axis SCARA robot in Epson Robots' LS-C line, rated for a 3 kg (8 kg maximum) payload with 500, 600 or 700 mm arm-length options and +/-0.02 mm repeatability. It runs on the RC800A controller with SafeSense technology and is offered in standard or ISO Class 4 cleanroom/ESD configurations for assembly and pick-and-place work.

The T6-B is an all-in-one 4-axis SCARA robot from Epson Robots with its controller built into the robot base, a 2 kg rated (6 kg maximum) payload, 600 mm arm reach and +/-0.04 mm repeatability. Running on single-phase 100-240 VAC power with no separate control cabinet, it is aimed at compact assembly and pick-and-place cells.

The C8LC is a long-reach six-axis industrial robot arm in Epson Robots' C-series, rated for a 3 kg (8 kg maximum) payload with a 981 mm reach to the flange and +/-0.03 mm repeatability. It runs on the RC800A controller with SafeSense technology, with standard and IP67-protected variants offered for material handling and assembly tasks.

The Flexion N6 is a compact six-axis industrial robot arm in Epson Robots' N-Series, using what Epson calls the world's first folding-arm design to reduce intermediate motion points and shorten cycle times versus conventional arms of similar size. It is rated for a 3 kg (6 kg maximum) payload with 850 mm or 1,000 mm reach options, +/-0.04 mm repeatability and a 69 kg weight, programmed through Epson RC+ software.

MELFA ASSISTA is Mitsubishi Electric's first collaborative robot, a 6-axis arm with a 5 kg payload, 900 mm reach and a claimed +/-0.02 mm repeatability, which the company positioned as comparable to its industrial-grade robots rather than typical +/-1 mm cobots. It runs at up to 250 mm/s in standard safety mode with a faster co-operative mode available, and launched in the UK in Q1 2020 at around 26,000 GBP.

The RV-4FR is a vertically articulated six-axis industrial robot arm in Mitsubishi Electric's RV-FR series, rated for a 4 kg payload with a 514.5 mm maximum reach. It is offered with MELSEC iQ-R, MELSEC Q or standalone controller options, plus standard, oil-mist and cleanroom environmental variants, for material handling and general industrial automation tasks.

The RV-13FR is a vertically articulated six-axis industrial robot arm in Mitsubishi Electric's RV-FR series, rated for a 13 kg payload with a 1094 mm maximum reach. It is offered with MELSEC iQ-R, MELSEC Q or standalone controller options, plus standard, oil-mist and cleanroom environmental variants, for material handling and general industrial automation tasks.

The RV-20FR is a vertically articulated six-axis industrial robot arm in Mitsubishi Electric's RV-FR series, rated for a 20 kg payload with a 1094 mm maximum reach. It is offered with MELSEC iQ-R, MELSEC Q or standalone controller options, plus standard, oil-mist and cleanroom environmental variants, for material handling and general industrial automation tasks.

The RV-50FR is a vertically articulated six-axis industrial robot arm in Mitsubishi Electric's RV-FR series, rated for a 50 kg payload with a 2100 mm maximum reach. It is offered with MELSEC iQ-R, MELSEC Q or standalone controller options, plus standard, oil-mist and cleanroom environmental variants, for material handling and general industrial automation tasks.

The RH-6FRH is a 4-axis SCARA robot in Mitsubishi Electric's MELFA RH-FRH series, rated for a 6 kg payload with 350, 450 or 550 mm maximum reach options. It is offered with MELSEC iQ-R or MELSEC Q controller compatibility and in standard, oil-mist and cleanroom environmental variants for assembly and handling tasks.

The RH-20CRH is a ceiling-mounted collaborative SCARA robot in Mitsubishi Electric's MELFA RH-CRH series, rated for a 20 kg payload with 850 or 1,000 mm reach options, running on a standalone controller. It is sold alongside the smaller 10 kg RH-10CRH for horizontal-articulated handling tasks requiring human-robot collaboration.

The VS-060 is a compact five/six-axis industrial robot arm from Denso Wave, with a 605 mm maximum arm reach, 4 kg maximum payload and a 0.35-second cycle time. It is positioned as a smaller, faster successor to Denso's original VS series for space-saving assembly and handling cells.

The VS-087 is a compact five/six-axis industrial robot arm from Denso Wave, with a 905 mm maximum arm reach, 7 kg maximum payload and a 0.34-second cycle time. It shares the downsized, high-speed body of the VS-068/087 pair, aimed at space-constrained assembly and handling applications.

The VP-6242 is a compact six-axis industrial robot arm from Denso Wave, built for confined work areas with a 432 mm maximum arm reach and a 2.5 kg maximum payload. It is sold alongside the five-axis VP-5243 (3 kg payload) in Denso's VP series for multi-directional handling in tight spaces.

The VM-60B1 is a slim-bodied six-axis industrial robot arm from Denso Wave with a 13 kg maximum payload, 1,298 mm maximum arm reach and a 0.95-second cycle time. It is offered in dust/splash-proof and cleanroom variants alongside the shorter-reach VM-6083 for large-work-area handling tasks.

The HSR-065 is the largest model in Denso Wave's HSR series of 4-axis SCARA robots, with a 650 mm total arm length, up to 510 mm vertical stroke, 8 kg maximum payload and a 0.31-second cycle time. It is marketed for high-speed assembly and handling, sharing the line with the shorter-reach HSR-048 and HSR-055.

The MZ04 is a six-axis industrial robot arm from Nachi-Fujikoshi, rated for a 4 kg payload with a 541 mm reach, weighing 26 kg. It is marketed for machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing applications.

The MZ07 is a six-axis industrial robot arm from Nachi-Fujikoshi, rated for a 7 kg payload with a 723 mm reach, weighing 36 kg. It is marketed for machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing applications.

The MZ12 is a six-axis industrial robot arm from Nachi-Fujikoshi, rated for a 12 kg payload with a 1454 mm reach, weighing 150 kg. It is marketed for machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing applications.

The MZ25 is a six-axis industrial robot arm from Nachi-Fujikoshi, rated for a 25 kg payload with a 1882 mm reach, weighing 250 kg. It is marketed for machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing applications.

The MZ50F is a six-axis industrial robot arm from Nachi-Fujikoshi, rated for a 50 kg payload with a 2102 mm reach, weighing 608 kg. It is marketed for machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing applications.

The TM5-900 is a six-axis collaborative robot in Techman Robot's TM AI Cobot series (sold by Omron as the TM series), with a built-in machine-vision camera in the arm, a 4 kg payload, 946 mm reach and 22 kg weight. It is marketed for assembly automation and inspection tasks that benefit from integrated vision.

The TM12 is a six-axis collaborative robot in Techman Robot's TM AI Cobot series (sold by Omron as the TM series), with a 12 kg payload and a 1,300 mm reach, among the longest in the TM lineup. It targets industrial-precision collaborative lifting and handling tasks.

The TM14 is a six-axis collaborative robot in Techman Robot's TM AI Cobot series (sold by Omron as the TM series), rated for a 14 kg payload with a 1,100 mm reach and 33 kg weight. It is built for heavier end-of-arm tooling and demanding, repetitive industrial operations.

The TM20 is the heavy-duty flagship of Techman Robot's TM AI Cobot series (sold by Omron as the TM series), with a 20 kg payload and 1,300 mm reach. It is aimed at large-scale pick-and-place, heavy machine tending and high-volume packaging applications.

The TM6S is a long-reach model in Techman Robot's newer TM AI Cobot S Series, with a 6 kg payload, 1,800 mm reach, 35 kg weight and IP65 protection. It is designed for applications needing wide workspace coverage with consistent precision.

The IRB 6730S is a shelf-mounted, high-payload six-axis industrial robot arm that ABB Robotics launched at Automatica 2025, rated for up to 350 kg payload. It is aimed at die casting, injection molding and spot welding in automotive, foundry and general manufacturing.

The IRB 6750S is a shelf-mounted, high-payload six-axis industrial robot arm that ABB Robotics launched at Automatica 2025, rated for up to 350 kg payload with 0.9 mm path accuracy on ABB's OmniCore controller and about 20% lower energy use than its IRB 6650S-200/3.0 predecessor. It is aimed at die casting, injection molding and spot welding in automotive, foundry and general manufacturing.

The IRB 6760 is a press-tending industrial robot arm that ABB Robotics launched at Automatica 2025, able to perform up to 15 strokes per minute (900 parts per hour) using a carbon-fiber tooling boom. It is aimed at automotive, electronics and general-manufacturing press lines.

The LR Mate 200iD is FANUC's small six-axis industrial robot arm series, reaching up to 911 mm with a maximum 7 kg payload and a calculated TCP speed of up to 11 m/s. It is sold in multiple variants (including washdown and cleanroom-oriented versions) for light assembly, pick-and-place and material-handling tasks.

The YK400XE is a compact SCARA robot in Yamaha Motor's YK-XE series, with a 400 mm arm reach and 4 kg maximum payload, built for low-cost, high-performance assembly, packaging and palletizing. It runs on Yamaha's RCX340 controller with support for CC-Link, EtherNet/IP, DeviceNet, PROFIBUS, PROFINET and EtherCAT field networks.

The YK610XE is a mid-size SCARA robot in Yamaha Motor's YK-XE series, with a 610 mm arm reach and 10 kg maximum payload, built for low-cost, high-performance assembly, packaging and palletizing. It runs on Yamaha's RCX340 controller with support for CC-Link, EtherNet/IP, DeviceNet, PROFIBUS, PROFINET and EtherCAT field networks.

The A0912 is a collaborative robot arm in Doosan Robotics' A-series, rated for a 9 kg payload with a 1200 mm reach and +/-0.05 mm repeatability, using torque sensors on every axis. It is aimed at general-purpose industrial automation, with force-sensor and food-and-beverage-specific (F) variants available.

The M0609 is a collaborative robot arm in Doosan Robotics' M-series, rated for a 6 kg payload with a 900 mm reach and +/-0.03 mm repeatability, using torque sensors on every axis. It is part of Doosan's Masterpiece (M) series for precision electronics and automotive machine-tending and assembly tasks.

The M1013 is a collaborative robot arm in Doosan Robotics' M-series, rated for a 10 kg payload with a 1300 mm reach and +/-0.05 mm repeatability, using torque sensors on every axis. It is part of Doosan's Masterpiece (M) series for precision electronics and automotive machine-tending and assembly tasks.

The H2515 is a collaborative robot arm in Doosan Robotics' H-series, rated for a 25 kg payload with a 1500 mm reach and +/-0.1 mm repeatability, using torque sensors on every axis. It is part of Doosan's High-Power (H) series, built for long-distance palletizing and heavy-duty logistics work.

The KR 6 R900-2 is a small six-axis industrial robot arm in KUKA's KR AGILUS family, rated for a 6 kg payload with a 901 mm reach. It is one of the best-known compact industrial arms sold for high-speed handling, assembly and packaging, offered in standard, cleanroom, hygienic, waterproof and explosion-proof variants across the AGILUS range.

The KR 210 is a heavy-payload six-axis industrial robot arm in KUKA's KR QUANTEC family, rated for a 210 kg payload with a reach between 2,701 and 3,305 mm depending on configuration. It is built for high-load material handling, spot welding and general industrial automation, with standard, console and foundry construction variants.

The MyCo-30-1.80 is the newest, heaviest-payload model in Comau's MyCo collaborative robot family, rated for a 30 kg maximum wrist payload with a 1,800 mm horizontal reach, 93 kg robot weight and +/-0.05 mm repeatability. It is IP54 rated (IP66 optional) and combines collaborative safety features with ergonomic benefits for floorspace-efficient human-robot work.

The Rebel-S6-0.60 is a 4-axis SCARA robot in Comau's Rebel-S family, rated for a 6 kg payload with a 600 mm horizontal reach, 200 mm vertical Z-stroke and +/-0.02 mm X-Y repeatability. It is offered for base or wall mounting and is sold alongside the smaller Rebel-S6-0.45 and larger Rebel-S6-0.75 in the line.

Kinova Gen3 is an ultra-lightweight 6- or 7-DoF robotic arm built for robotics research, with an embedded 2D/3D vision module and 1 kHz closed-loop control. It reaches 891 mm, weighs 7.2 kg, draws 36 W and carries up to 4 kg mid-range continuous payload, and is used by universities and labs worldwide for manipulation research.

Kinova Gen3 lite is a compact, accessible 6-DoF research robotic arm with an underactuated two-finger gripper. It weighs 5.4 kg, reaches 760 mm, moves at up to 25 cm/s, carries a 0.5 kg mid-range continuous payload and is rated IP22.

OMX-AI is ROBOTIS' open-source leader-follower robotic arm bundle for Physical AI research, pairing a 5-DOF-plus-gripper OMX-L leader arm (335 mm reach, 360 g) with an OMX-F follower arm (400 mm reach, 560 g, up to 250 g payload). It is ROS 2 compatible and built for teleoperation data collection and imitation-learning workflows in robotics education and labs.

OMY-3M is ROBOTIS' 6-DOF research robotic arm with native ROS 2 (ros2_control) support for real-time control, simulation and reinforcement learning. It carries a 3 kg payload at up to 580 mm reach with +-0.05 mm repeatability, weighs 13.5 kg and runs on high-precision DYNAMIXEL-Y actuators.

CR7HT is a high-performance collaborative robot in Dobot's new CRH series, announced in November 2026 at Dobot's Robotics Ecosystem Conference in Frankfurt.
